entries.search: Eight mammography trials, re-read against Danish data, put screening overdiagnosis below 5 percent A meta-analysis in JNCI Journal of the National Cancer Institute reanalysed all eight mammography screening trials against two Danish regional programmes and found that the excess of detected cancers matches the Danish level, where overdiagnosis is put below 5 percent. Sisse Helle Njor of the University of Southern Denmark and her co-authors argue that earlier estimates of 30-50 percent were built on trial data that had not matured; the work generates no new screening data of its own. science Science Science 2026-09-14 Eight trials read against a Danish yardstick Three adjustments turned a 30-50 percent estimate into under 5 percent What the authors say it means for women invited to screening A reanalysis of eight mammography trials puts breast screening overdiagnosis below 5 percent EurekAlert! entries.search: Eight years on, three years of osimertinib after surgery lifts lung cancer survival to 74 percent In ADAURA, a phase III trial of osimertinib taken for up to three years after surgery for EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer, 74 percent of stage II-IIIA patients on the drug were alive at eight years against 58 percent of those without it; across stages IB-IIIA the figures were 79 percent and 64 percent. entries.search: In the most polluted areas glaucoma odds run up to 70 percent higher, across 41 pooled studies A meta-analysis of 41 observational studies from East Asia and the United Kingdom, presented by Ahmed Alnabihi of Riyadh's King Khaled Eye Specialist Hospital at the ESCRS congress in London, finds glaucoma and cataract more common where air pollution is higher. The clearest link is with fine particles: each step up in exposure went with around 8 percent more glaucoma risk and 4 percent more cataract risk, and the most polluted areas had up to 70 percent higher glaucoma odds. entries.search: Six months outside the ISS left most intraocular lenses intact, but every light-adjustable lens came back altered In the JAMES experiment, 135 intraocular lenses spent about six months mounted on the outside of the International Space Station without packaging. Of the 61 examined so far, 42 showed no change linked to exposure; eight of nine acrylic lenses in the carrier facing the direction of flight cracked, five lenses yellowed, and the six light-adjustable lenses all came back with a cobblestone texture whose origin is still unknown. Morgan Micheletti presented the results at the ESCRS congress in London as an exploratory step towards eye surgery in space. science Science Science 2026-09-14 135 lenses rode outside the station for six months Acrylics cracked facing the flight direction; every light-adjustable lens came back cobblestoned An exploratory first step, with surgical equipment next in line Most intraocular lenses survived six months outside the ISS, while all six light-adjustable lenses came back altered EurekAlert!

entries.search: Webb sees Chariklo's inner ring thicken by 50 percent while its outer ring fades by 60 percent A James Webb Space Telescope stellar occultation in October 2022 shows the two narrow rings of Chariklo, a Centaur about 250 kilometres across, changing in opposite directions: the inner ring blocks about 50 percent more starlight than in earlier occultations, while the outer ring's signal is about 60 percent weaker than in 2017. The result narrows models of its cooling interior and gives the approaching BepiColombo observations a revised benchmark for more detailed surface measurements.
entries.title: Impact debris hid evidence that lifts Mercury's diameter loss to about 19 kilometres

Nautilus reports the team traced this to the whimper's alarm function and compared it with human vocal development, where laughter varies more across languages than distress calls.

Eastern waters held three of the four critically endangered species detected. Jessica Pearce's team presents the survey as input for marine-park management in a gulf still pulled by competing interests.
entries.title: Exmouth Gulf's east holds 3 of 4 critically endangered species found in an eDNA survey

entries.search: Fraunhofer IOF built an 85-micrometre double slit for ESA's FLEX fluorescence spectrometer Fraunhofer IOF in Jena has described the silicon double-slit assembly and two high-precision mirrors it built for FLORIS, the imaging spectrometer on ESA's FLEX mission, set to launch on 15 September 2026. Each slit is 85 micrometres wide over 44.15 millimetres. entries.search: MIT team rules out the neutrino laser: recoil and fermionic nature close the path Wolfgang Ketterle, Hanzhen Lin and Yu-Kun Lu show in two Physical Review Letters papers that last year's neutrino laser proposal cannot be built. entries.search: Nature retracts its global drought paper after the authors found the error in their own code Nature published a retraction note on 2 September for the paper that appeared online on 4 June 2025 and concluded global drought is accelerating. The authors write that after being notified of errors they found further problems themselves: averages that were not area-weighted, results from an older evaporation model in one figure, a timestepping error in the code computing regional drought areas, and an unexplained masking method. entries.search: USS Abraham Lincoln docked in Thailand after 250 days without a port call The nuclear-powered aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln entered Laem Chabang port in Thailand on Wednesday, giving its roughly 5,000 crew their first break ashore. It calls the NPT right to peaceful nuclear energy inalienable, offers condolences over Seyyed Ali Khamenei, and opposes unilateral coercive measures. geopolitics Geopolitics Geopolitics 2026-09-01 Ten members sign the joint text in Bishkek The Bishkek Declaration writes a diplomatic path and condolences NPT rights, unilateral measures and the Palestine clause SCO leaders sign a Bishkek Declaration condemning the strikes on Iran and backing its NPT rights Al Jazeera SCO condemns US strikes on Iran as a breach of international law and the UN Charter The New Indian Express
entries.summary: The ten members of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation signed the Bishkek Declaration at the close of a two-day summit in the Kyrgyz capital. It calls the NPT right to peaceful nuclear energy inalienable, offers condolences over Seyyed Ali Khamenei, and opposes unilateral coercive measures.

entries.search: The UAE intercepts an Iranian drone and denies a strike on Al Minhad The United Arab Emirates said it intercepted an Iranian drone over its territorial waters, calling it a blatant violation of sovereignty. The Defence Ministry separately dismissed an Iranian army claim of a strike on the Al Minhad Air Base in Dubai as false. Iran claimed the attack on Al Minhad was in retaliation for the killing of its Revolutionary Guards and civilians on Larak Island during renewed fire between the US and Iran. geopolitics Geopolitics Geopolitics 2026-09-01 The UAE says it intercepted an Iranian drone over its territorial waters The Defence Ministry denies an Iranian claim of a strike on Al Minhad Air Base Iran links the attempted strike to deaths on Larak Island The UAE rejects Iran's claim on the Al Minhad base and announces a drone interception AP News The UAE engaged an Iranian drone over its waters and denied the Al Minhad strike claim Onmanorama

entries.search: Trump leaves the US line on Falklands sovereignty open Donald Trump told reporters he reviews every position when asked whether he was reconsidering US support for British sovereignty over the Falkland Islands. Washington officially takes no side but practically recognises British administration. The review is reportedly part of Pentagon measures to incentivise NATO allies like the UK to hit a 5 percent defence spending target. An unnamed US official separately suggested the stance could change if Britain missed defence spending commitments. geopolitics Geopolitics Geopolitics 2026-09-01 Trump says the Falklands stance is one of many positions under review The Pentagon prepares measures to push NATO allies toward a 5 percent spending target Healey prepares to drop the 3 percent defence pledge Trump signals a review of the US stance on the Falklands The Guardian Trump put the US position on the Falkland Islands under review The Straits Times

entries.search: US House leaders keep Graham's Russia sanctions act off this week's vote list Republican leaders in the US House left the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia Act off this week's vote list after a five-week recess. The Senate passed it 86 to 11; Kyiv Post dates that vote to 7 August. Virginia Foxx told POLITICO nobody was talking about the bill, and Mike Johnson gave no date. Kyiv Post says the act would let the president impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on goods from countries buying Russian oil, gas and uranium. geopolitics Geopolitics Geopolitics 2026-09-01 US House leaders leave Graham's act off this week's vote list Senate-passed act would put tariffs on Russia's commodity buyers Election calendar and a House split leave a floor vote uncertain House leaders leave Graham's Russia sanctions act off this week's floor schedule POLITICO The Graham sanctions act, passed 86-11 by the Senate, waits in the House Kyiv Post

entries.search: XENONnT catches the faintest solar neutrino collisions yet measured The XENON collaboration announced on 31 August 2026 that XENONnT recorded the faintest neutrino collisions: solar neutrinos scattering off electrons beneath a mountain in central Italy. The observation stands at 5 sigma, with less than a one in a million chance of a fluke, and reaches about 17 keV. pp neutrinos from the fusion that powers the Sun dominate the record. The 5.9 tonne liquid xenon chamber, built to hunt dark matter 1,400 metres under Gran Sasso, now sees solar neutrinos as an irreducible background for that search. science Science Science 2026-09-01 XENONnT measures solar neutrinos scattering off electrons for the first time Kobayashi calls the result an important step for low-energy neutrino physics Direct neutrino observations now reach about 17 keV XENONnT catches solar boron-8 neutrinos and runs into the fog they make Scientific American LNGS's XENONnT sees solar neutrinos scatter off electrons down to about 17 keV AZoQuantum
